research_question: What is the effect of a higher (liberal) fraction of inspired oxygen or arterial oxygenation target, compared with a lower (conservative) target, on all-cause mortality in adults admitted to the intensive care unit?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality at longest reported follow-up (number of deaths divided by total randomised participants in each arm)
positive_direction: Higher mortality risk (more deaths) in the higher (liberal) oxygen target group compared to the lower (conservative) oxygen target group
search_queries: liberal conservative oxygen targets intensive care randomized trial mortality
hyperoxia normoxia mechanical ventilation critically ill trial mortality
higher lower oxygenation target ICU randomized controlled trial mortality
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials evaluating higher (liberal) versus lower (conservative) oxygen or arterial oxygenation targets in adult ICU patients
Reports all-cause mortality at the longest available follow-up for both treatment arms
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols)
No comparison between higher (liberal) and lower (conservative) oxygen or oxygenation targets, or evaluating hyperbaric oxygen or different delivery devices at identical targets
No quantitative all-cause mortality data reported to calculate a risk ratio
Pediatric or neonatal populations (age under 18 years) or studies completely unrelated to intensive care oxygenation targets
moderators_to_extract: ICU patient population (post-cardiac arrest, ARDS/hypoxemic respiratory failure, sepsis/septic shock, undifferentiated mechanical ventilation)
Oxygen target metric and separation (target SpO2 or PaO2 ranges in liberal vs conservative arms)
Timing of mortality outcome (e.g., hospital discharge, 28/30 days, 90 days, 180 days)
effect_size_note: Pool as risk ratio (RR) using random-effects model. RR > 1 indicates higher risk of all-cause mortality with the higher (liberal) oxygen target. Denominator is total randomised participants (ITT), using the longest follow-up reported.
